text:
ajay: Heads-up — after yesterday's EU preemption spike we should revisit autoscaler settings for spot-backed inference pools. saw 27% interruption rate on p4d-spot in eu-west-1 between 02:10-02:25 :grimacing:

maria: ugh, noticed latency bumps. how are we currently scaling?

ajay: Right now we scale on pendingRequests > 8 per nodegroup and set cooldown 60s. surge_control set to 0.15 (15%). no dedicated buffer.

liam: That's tight. For inference workloads I prefer a small on-demand buffer (5-10%) + higher surge for rapid scale-outs. Spots can vanish in bursts.

tara: Agree with liam. Also add an interruption handler to proactively drain affected replicas and shift traffic to fallbacks. We should use node-termination-handler and immediate cold-start fallback to on-demand.

ajay: Proposed quick config tweak: increase cooldown to 90s, surge_control 0.25, and keep 7% on-demand reserve for the EU pools. thoughts?

maria: +1 for reserve. Also recommend scale-out trigger be queue_length > 12 OR avg_replica_cpu > 70% for 30s, not just pending count. pending is noisy with short bursts.

liam: One more: use weighted mixed pools (spot weight=0.6, on-demand=0.4) and prefer spreading across AZs to reduce simultaneous preempts.

ajay: Sketching an autoscaler snippet (pseudo config):

```yaml
policy:
  scale_out:
    triggers:
      - type: queue_length
        threshold: 12
        duration: 30s
      - type: cpu
        threshold: 70%
        duration: 30s
  cooldowns:
    scale_out: 90s
    scale_in: 300s
  surge_control: 0.25
  on_demand_reserve: 0.07
  mixed_pool_weights: { spot: 0.6, on_demand: 0.4 }
```

oncall-carlos: +1. add a fast-retry path: if spot preemptions > 3 in 5m, temporarily raise on_demand_reserve to 20% for 10m. helps avoid repeated flapping.

maria: Good call. Also enable graceful shutdown timeout 60s on inference containers so KV caches can be checkpointed where possible.

liam: We should test with a chaos job that kills spot nodes according to the recent preempt pattern — verify scale-out and route-fallback within SLA.

ajay: I ran a quick simulation this morning. With surge_control 0.25 + 7% reserve, estimated cost increase ~+6% but availability jack up reducing 95p latency failures by ~80%. trade seems worth it for customer-facing tiers.

maria: Can you paste the sim command/log?

ajay: quick log: 
```
2025-12-08T02:12:03Z simulate-preempt --region eu-west-1 --pattern burst --nodes 120
result: preempted=33, time_to_recover_median=42s (with new config), fallback_to_ondemand=18 nodes
```

tara: Nice. For cost control add a surge_cap absolute limit as well (e.g., max extra 30 nodes) so spikes don't blow budget.

liam: Also set per-customer token-rate throttle in the service to avoid single-tenant storms causing scale cascades. we've seen that before.

ajay: To summarize action items:
- increase cooldowns (scale_out 90s) + surge_control 0.25
- add on_demand_reserve 7% (temporary 20% on repeated preempts)
- change triggers to queue_length OR cpu with 30s window
- graceful shutdown 60s, node-termination-handler enabled
- chaos test for spot kill patterns and a hard surge_cap (absolute nodes)

maria: I'll open an RFC and a small rollout playbook for eng-sre + runtime. include rollback steps to lower reserve if cost impact unacceptable.

oncall-carlos: I'll add alerting: spot_preempt_rate > 10% over 5m -> page + auto-escalate to raise reserve.

sre-bot: deploy-checklist created: /infra/ops/spot-autoscaler-tune (PR needed).

liam: Sounds good. When do we want to ship?

ajay: aiming for quick prod canary tonight in eu-west-1 on non-critical routes, full roll by end of week if canary ok. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone, will draft RFC and ping for review.

ajay: thanks — will post results of the chaos run here once complete.
